content_preview.title: LibreOffice 26.8 Sets New First-Week Download Record With Over 1 Million Downloads
content_preview.summary: The Document Foundation says LibreOffice 26.8 drew 1,031,162 downloads from its official site in its first week, the highest first-week figure for any LibreOffice release.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

LibreOffice 26.8 drew 1,031,162 downloads from the free office suite's official downloads page in its first seven days on the market, according to [The Document Foundation](https://blog.documentfoundation.org/blog/2026/09/02/one-week-of-libreoffice-26-8-the-stats/), which called it "the highest number of downloads in the first week of any LibreOffice release." editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (732 words, within the 400-1200 range). Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure used correctly and consistently with the site's format. The headline figure ('Over 1 Million Downloads') is a fair, conservative rounding of the precise 1,031,162 figure, which is given exactly in the summary and lead. The 'What We Don't Know' section is honest — it correctly notes that neither source gives a total download figure once distro repositories, Snap Store, Flathub and PPAs are counted, and that neither source addressed whether the surge reflects new installs versus updates. The Analysis section correctly hedges OMG! Ubuntu's AI-driven-the-surge theory as that outlet's own editorial speculation rather than a claim from The Document Foundation.

editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article appears verbatim in its cited snapshot (checked individually above). The headline's core number (1,031,162) is precisely and consistently sourced in both the Document Foundation stats post and independently corroborated by OMG! Ubuntu. No hallucinated figures, no misattributed quotes, no orphan source URLs (all 3 URLs in article.sources are used and correctly attributed in body_markdown).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No AI self-reference. The one place the article ventures into interpretation (the AI-avoidance-drove-downloads theory) is correctly quarantined in the Analysis section and explicitly attributed as OMG! Ubuntu's own speculation, not asserted as fact.

Found no article covering this release or these download figures — the only prior LibreOffice mention (2026-07-15, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Nextcloud migration) is an unrelated public-sector-procurement story that references LibreOffice only in passing. Genuinely new topic, not a duplicate.
editor_notes.allowlist_gap: The automated script's only finding was a 'Sources not in allowlist' warning for omgubuntu.co.uk. OMG! Ubuntu is a long-running (since 2009), named-byline (Joey Sneddon) Ubuntu/Linux news outlet published by Ohso Media, directly comparable in tier to already-allowlisted Linux-focused outlets itsfoss.com and phoronix.com. Its content was verified verbatim against the snapshot during this review (see source_verification) and independently corroborates the Document Foundation's own figures rather than contradicting them. This is a source-allowlist completeness gap, not an actual sourcing or factual defect, directly analogous to the 2026-09-01 TIOBE review precedent (tiobe.com/techrepublic.com added, verdict overridden from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE). Added omgubuntu.co.uk to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justifying comment. Overriding script verdict from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — no corrections record is warranted since there is no factual or sourcing defect for a reader-facing corrections note to describe.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, thoroughly sourced News submission. All quotes and figures verified verbatim across all three snapshots, the headline figure is a fair rounding of a precisely-sourced number, the 'What We Don't Know' section is honest about the article's limits, and the one interpretive claim is correctly hedged and attributed. The only automated flag was a source-allowlist completeness gap for one legitimate, independently-corroborating outlet, which has been fixed at the allowlist level. Overriding script verdict from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — no corrections record warranted.
